text: Eleven lessons of deliverables need a permanent home. This lesson chooses the operating model that houses all of it going forward.

Fully centralized would make the small program team a bottleneck across three regions. Fully decentralized is what already existed before this program started. LTV Global lands on a federated hybrid model instead: a small central office for standards, domain owners keeping day-to-day authority.

Four layers: Dana Whitfield as executive sponsor, Marcus Ibe's governance office running the KPIs and glossary, the four domain owners keeping Lesson 4's accountability, and their stewards doing the daily work. A monthly Data Governance Council is where escalations land.

Nothing from this chapter was a one-time document. The landscape inventory and glossary are maintained, not frozen. CDE scoring and classification get revisited, as DateOfBirth already proved. Quality rules, lineage, and access policy stay with their owners, reviewed monthly.
This closes the foundational half of the capstone. Next: Lesson 13 builds an AI governance strategy on top of the structure this lesson just made permanent.
